notes: These arcs began as canon-grounded pressures at the campaign start. They do not precommit future victories, deaths, promotions, meetings, or chronology. Player and NPC actions may delay, redirect, transform, or prevent later arcs. Every active arc has a real owner and next review. Dormant arcs activate only when their saved prerequisites become true.

facts.current_basis: Qin and Wei face an era-defining contest over the strategic Sanyou region when the 242 BCE campaign year is reached; the pressure must enter play but no historical victor, commander, casualty, promotion, or territorial result is guaranteed.
facts.information_path: military dispatches, court reports, merchants and frontier movement
facts.possible_results: Qin offensive, Wei preemption, negotiated pause, transformed regional campaign, failed mobilization, siege, field battle, withdrawal, or other causally supported divergence

state_qin.goal: Contest the strategically valuable Sanyou region in Wei if Qin authority, forces, routes, logistics, and politics can sustain the campaign.

state_wei.goal: Defend Wei territory and the Sanyou strategic region against Qin campaign pressure using lawful forces, fortifications, diplomacy, and logistics.

protected_pressure.causal_impossibility_rule: The pressure may fail to take this form only if the required sovereigns no longer exist or material divergence makes the registered actor set impossible; failure never manufactures the historical outcome.

facts.current_basis: By the 241 BCE campaign year, surviving rival states face protected strategic pressure to coordinate against Qin. The coalition crisis must enter sovereign decision space, but membership, diplomacy, invasion routes, battles, deaths, defections, victories and final outcome are not scripted.
facts.information_path: sovereign diplomacy, intelligence reports, court dispatches, merchants and military mobilization
facts.possible_results: large coalition, partial coalition, failed negotiations, staggered invasions, independent containment campaigns, Qin diplomatic fracture of the coalition, transformed war, negotiated settlement, or other causally supported divergence

state_chu.goal: Coordinate with other surviving states to contain Qin and prepare a materially supportable response if coalition diplomacy succeeds or fails.

Arc settlement law
notes: A monthly world close cannot advance an arc merely because time passed. Each progression needs actor, action, target, means, authority, route, resources, opposition, and committed result evidence. If the player changes the prerequisites, canon becomes a reference trajectory rather than a forced script.
